assets.movement: downward dog to upward dog flow
prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame exercise animation sprite sheet for a fitness web app
Primary request: Show ONE complete DOWNWARD-FACING DOG to UPWARD-FACING DOG flow and return. Exactly 4 columns × 4 rows of equal panels, read left-to-right top-to-bottom. In all frames the same adult is on a gray mat facing image right, palms grounded at the same spot near the front of the mat. Frames 1–3 downward dog: straight arms, hands and feet on floor, hips pushed back and high making a clear inverted V, head relaxed between arms. Frames 4–8 transition: chest moves forward through the hands, hips descend, spine extends, feet turn so tops of shoes rest on mat. Frames 9–10 upward dog: straight arms, chest lifted and facing forward, shoulders down away from ears, hips low, legs extended. Frames 11–16 reverse the path smoothly back to the high-hip inverted V and end identical to frame 1. This must be a yoga flow, not push-ups.
Scene/backdrop: fixed light warm-gray studio, single gray exercise mat, no props.
Subject: one same anatomically plausible adult in mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers in each tile, not a stick figure.
Style/medium: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instruction render, crisp consistent camera and soft studio light.
Composition/framing: fixed clean side view slightly elevated, complete body including hands, head and both shoes wholly inside every tile with generous margin; identical person scale and mat position in each tile; seamless edge-to-edge 4×4 contact sheet, no gutters.
Constraints: exactly 16 equal row-major tiles, one person per tile, visible major change from high-hip dog to low-hip chest-up dog and back, grounded palms throughout, no extra limbs.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, arrows, borders, gridlines, watermark, blank panels, clipped limbs, normal plank or push-up.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: corrected 16-frame Down Dog ↔ Up Dog flow sprite sheet
Input image: supplied seamless 4×4 yoga flow contact sheet is edit target.
Primary request: Correct UPWARD DOG form in ONLY frames 6–11 (row 2 columns 2–4, row 3 columns 1–3), including the intermediate transition. In frames 7–10 of the up-dog hold, palms and TOPS OF FEET are the only contact points. Lift pelvis, thighs and both knees several centimeters ABOVE the mat, with a visible band of background/shadow gap beneath the thighs and knees. Arms stay straight, chest lifts forward and up, shoulders stay down. Frame 6 can be a lower transition but knees already beginning to float. Frame 11 remains descending back through plank with knees floating. Do not make cobra pose: abdomen, thighs, knees must not rest on the mat in up dog. Keep feet on the mat and full body in each tile.
Preserve exactly: frames 1–5 and 12–16; 4×4 tile layout and aspect; same adult gray shirt/charcoal shorts/gray shoes, same fixed side camera, mat, studio, lighting and framing. Maintain row-major down dog→up dog→down dog cycle.
Avoid: changing start/end high-hip inverted V, text, numbers, arrows, borders, gutter, blank cells, cropped limbs, extra limbs.
assets.assessment: 4x4 fixed side view; high-hip down dog through forward transition to palms/tops-of-feet-supported upward dog with knees and thighs visibly above mat, then back to down dog.
assets.caveats: First candidate showed thighs down (cobra-like); repaired middle frames. Native output aspect is landscape, so the sixteen equal cells are rectangular.

prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame exercise animation sprite sheet for a fitness web app
Primary request: Show a complete BILATERAL PIGEON POSE stretch sequence, left front leg then right front leg, in exactly 16 ordered frames in 4 columns × 4 rows. In pigeon pose one FRONT knee is flexed in front of the hips with its shin lying across the mat; the OPPOSITE back leg is straight behind with top of shoe resting on mat, hips mostly square. Person slowly folds chest forward over front shin then lifts up. Frames 1–3 LEFT knee is the front bent leg and RIGHT leg extends behind, torso upright with palms planted beside hips. Frames 4–6 same LEFT-front pigeon, chest folds down gently and holds. Frames 7–8 lifts torso and comes briefly to hands-and-knees center to change legs. Frames 9–11 RIGHT knee is the front bent leg and LEFT leg extends straight behind, torso upright. Frames 12–14 same RIGHT-front pigeon, chest folds gently over right shin and holds. Frames 15–16 torso lifts and finishes in neutral hands-and-knees. Left-front and right-front leg arrangement must clearly differ, and no extra legs.
Scene/backdrop: fixed light warm-gray studio, single gray exercise mat, no props.
Subject: same one adult in plain mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers every tile, anatomically plausible human, no stick figure.
Style: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instruction render with soft studio light.
Composition: fixed elevated FRONT THREE-QUARTER view looking diagonally down so bent front shin and straight back leg are visible, full body including hands, head, both shoes entirely inside each tile with margin; identical scale and camera every tile. Seamless edge-to-edge contact sheet, exactly 4×4 equal panels, no gutter.
Constraints: correct pigeon pose left front then right front, shoulders and hips squared, no extra limbs, row-major motion.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, arrows, borders, gridlines, watermark, blank panels, clipped limbs, seated cross-legged pose, both knees bent behind.
assets.assessment: 4x4 fixed three-quarter view; first bent front shin with opposite straight leg, folds, returns to hands and knees, mirrors leg configuration, folds, returns.
assets.caveats: Some shoe tips are near panel edges. Native output aspect makes equal cells rectangular.

prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame exercise animation sprite sheet for a fitness web app
Primary request: Show ONE complete SUPERMAN ROW repetition, exactly 16 frames in a 4 columns × 4 rows equal-panel contact sheet, read left-to-right then top-to-bottom. Adult lies prone face down on exercise mat, pelvis and thighs on mat, chest only SLIGHTLY lifted (small upper back extension) and neck neutral, legs straight behind. Both arms start reaching straight forward overhead, hovering just above floor. The rowing action pulls BOTH bent elbows backward toward the ribs while shoulder blades squeeze; hands travel from forward reach to beside the lower chest/rib cage. Then both arms extend forward again. Frames 1–3 forward reach; 4–8 gradual row with elbows moving rearward and shoulder blades drawing together; 9–10 elbows back by ribs; 11–16 extend arms forward to original pose. No equipment. Torso lift remains small and controlled; legs stay down. This is a ROW with bent elbows and visible hand translation, not a snow-angel sweep.
Scene: fixed light warm-gray studio, single gray mat, no props.
Subject: same one adult in plain mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers in every tile, anatomically plausible, no stick figures.
Style: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instruction render, consistent fixed camera and soft light.
Composition: fixed elevated side three-quarter angle that shows chest lift and both elbow positions, whole body including hands, head and both shoes within every tile with generous margin; same scale and mat placement, seamless 4×4 edge-to-edge contact sheet, no gutters.
Constraints: exactly 16 ordered tiles, one person per tile, small chest lift, bilateral elbow row and release, no extra limbs.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, arrows, borders, gridlines, watermark, blank panels, clipped limbs, high Superman back bend, hands sweeping wide like snow angels, arms staying straight throughout.

Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: corrected 16-frame Superman Row fitness animation sheet
Input image: supplied seamless 4×4 Superman Row sheet is edit target.
Primary request: Create CLEARLY PROGRESSIVE intermediate arm positions in this row-major cycle while preserving the correct prone movement. Change arm angles and elbow bends in the many duplicated panels. Frames 1–2 both arms fully reaching forward; frames 3–7, in five distinct stages, both elbows bend and draw backward while hands travel from in front of head toward ribs and shoulder blades retract; frames 8–9 elbows fully back beside ribs at row peak; frames 10–14, in five distinct reverse stages, elbows extend and hands travel forward again; frames 15–16 fully reaching forward like frame 1. Adjacent moving stages must visibly differ. Keep the torso only slightly raised with chest hovering, pelvis/thighs down, neck neutral. Bilateral symmetric rowing, not alternating arms.
Preserve: same adult gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers, exact 4×4 equal tile contact sheet, fixed side three-quarter view, mat, background, lighting, full-body framing, no equipment.
Avoid: repeated static hold taking most of sheet, big Superman back extension, wide snow angel sweep, text, numbers, arrows, borders, gutters, blank panels, clipped extremities, extra limbs.

Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame fitness exercise animation contact sheet
Primary request: Show ONE complete SUPERMAN ROW rep as 16 DISTINCT sequential frames in 4 columns × 4 rows, reading left-to-right then top-to-bottom. The same adult lies PRONE face down, abdomen/pelvis/legs on mat, chest only a LITTLE lifted and neck neutral. Both arms hover. First hands are far FORWARD beyond head, with straight elbows. Then BOTH elbows simultaneously bend and pull REARWARD toward RIBS, hands coming to the sides of rib cage while shoulder blades retract. Then arms slowly extend FORWARD again. This is a rowing action, not a snow-angel lateral sweep.
FRAME-BY-FRAME ARM DISTANCES from the head in row-major order:
1 full forward reach, 2 90% reach, 3 75% reach, 4 60% reach,
5 45% reach with more elbow bend, 6 30% reach, 7 15% reach,
8 hands beside ribs/elbows fully pulled back, 9 same peak,
10 15% reach, 11 30%, 12 45%, 13 60%, 14 75%, 15 90%, 16 full forward reach again.
Every stage should visibly change the position of BOTH hands and elbows, yielding a smooth loop. Keep torso almost still; no huge arch.
Scene: simple fixed light gray studio, one gray mat, no props or equipment.
Subject: same adult in gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers, realistic anatomy.
Style: polished naturalistic 3D instructional render, consistent light.
Composition: fixed camera directly overhead looking at the BACK with HEAD AT TOP and feet bottom in each tile. Body and fully forward reaching fingertips fit inside every tile with ample margin, identical scale, no cropped limbs. Exactly 4×4 seamless equal panels edge-to-edge, no gutter.
Avoid: text, labels, numbers, arrows, grid lines, borders, watermark, blank cells, extra limbs, alternating arms, hands sweeping sideways, chest or legs strongly lifting.
assets.assessment: 4x4 overhead view; visibly progressive bilateral elbow bend and hand retraction from overhead reach toward ribs, then progressive return to reach.
assets.caveats: Overhead camera makes slight chest lift less visible than the side-view rejected variants. Earlier two variants had long duplicated holds.

prompts:
Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: 16-frame exercise animation sprite sheet for a fitness web app
Primary request: Show ONE complete PRONE REVERSE SNOW ANGEL repetition in exactly 16 ordered frames, laid out as 4 columns × 4 rows of equal panels, read left-to-right top-to-bottom. Adult lies face-down on a gray mat, abdomen/chest/pelvis and straight legs stay grounded; head neutral facing floor. Both arms float just a few centimeters above mat, almost straight with slight natural elbow softness. Starting with hands beside the THIGHS, simultaneously sweep both arms OUT in a very wide lateral arc past shoulder-height T, then continue overhead until hands nearly meet above the head in a wide Y, then sweep the arms back along the same wide arc to the thighs. Frames 1–2 hands by thighs; 3–5 arms opening to T; 6–8 arms continuing to full overhead Y; 9–10 hold overhead; 11–14 arms returning through T; 15–16 hands beside thighs. Make a FULL large arc reaching OVERHEAD. This is longer range than half floor angel and not a row: elbows do not pull into ribs.
Scene: fixed light warm-gray studio, single gray mat, no props.
Subject: same one adult in plain mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers every tile, anatomically plausible, no stick figure.
Style: polished naturalistic 3D exercise instructional render, fixed consistent directly overhead camera and soft studio light.
Composition: full body including hands, head and both shoes entirely inside every tile with ample margin for the overhead reach; identical scale and position across tiles; seamless edge-to-edge 4×4 contact sheet, no gutters.
Constraints: exactly 16 ordered tiles; one person per tile; grounded torso, small hovering arm sweep hips→T→overhead Y→T→hips, no extra limbs.
Avoid: text, numbers, labels, arrows, borders, gridlines, watermark, blank panels, clipped fingers or shoes, Superman back extension, rowing elbows, bent-elbow W endpoint.

Use case: scientific-educational
Asset type: corrected 16-frame reverse snow angel exercise sprite sheet
Primary request: Make a NEW full-range PRONE REVERSE SNOW ANGEL 4×4 animation contact sheet (16 equal panels row-major). Same adult lies face-down, chest, pelvis, legs grounded; both mostly straight arms hover inches above mat and trace one CONTINUOUS BIG ARC from hands beside THIGHS outward through a horizontal T to FULLY FORWARD OVERHEAD, palms reaching beyond the head close to parallel with the ears, then trace the same arc backward to thighs.
Exact sequence of both arm positions (relative to long body axis): frames 1–2 hands beside hips pointing toward feet; frame 3 diagonal low outward (about 45° away from hips); frame 4 horizontal T; frames 5–6 diagonal forward high; frames 7–9 BOTH ARMS STRAIGHT FORWARD PAST HEAD, palms close parallel near ears at the overhead peak; frames 10–11 diagonal forward high; frame 12 horizontal T; frame 13 diagonal low outward; frames 14–16 hands return beside hips. Do not end at a wide Y; go all the way past the head with arms nearly parallel to the spine at the top.
Scene: fixed warm-gray studio, single gray mat.
Subject: anatomically plausible adult, mid-gray T-shirt, charcoal shorts, gray trainers, same in each tile.
Style: polished naturalistic 3D instruction image, soft consistent lighting.
Composition: fixed top-down overhead camera with HEAD TOWARD TOP OF EACH TILE and FEET TOWARD BOTTOM. Make the person/mat SMALL ENOUGH that feet and fully overhead fingertips all have generous blank background margin INSIDE every tile. Exactly 4×4 seamless edge-to-edge equal panels, no gutter.
Constraints: 16 ordered panels, single adult per panel, chest/legs remain down, arms change angle smoothly in both directions, no extra limbs.
Avoid: text, labels, numbers, borders, arrows, tile lines, watermark, blank tiles, any clipping at panel edges, bent-elbow row/W, chest or legs lifting.
assets.assessment: 4x4 overhead; arms trace gradual full arc from beside thighs through T to both hands forward past head close to parallel, then reverse; torso/legs grounded.
assets.caveats: Native output aspect yields equal rectangular cells. Initial candidate only reached wide Y and had shoes at edges; repaired.
